subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and reconcile app-owned LaunchAgent drift after updates, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats launchd/plist state as authoritative, while the requested fix would restore an enabled preference after app replacement; that choice affects user control, upgrade behavior, and how external disables are respected.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile app-owned drift
options.body: Store explicit in-app enablement and re-register only the OpenClaw-owned LaunchAgent after startup/update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave live launchd/System Settings state as the source of truth and document that OpenClaw will not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Hold implementation until a current-main Sparkle update repro identifies the exact state transition that flips the toggle.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile app-owned drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit in-app enablement and re-register only the OpenClaw-owned LaunchAgent after startup/update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses macOS app UX and launch-at-login persistence semantics, and steipete is the strongest owner signal from adjacent merged history.
